subject: Throughput profile: peak windows & streaming latency checkpoints
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Tim Hart <tim.hart@fastpay.com>, Asha Kapoor <asha.kapoor@fastpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Throughput profile: peak windows & streaming latency checkpoints

Hi Tim / Asha —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and a few targeted follow-ups so we can convert the discovery into a sizing + SLO proposal for your SREs and platform team.

Notes from the call:
- Product: realtime invoice ingestion + live reconciliation UI (streaming partial predictions back to the browser).
- Current integration: batch uploads + webhook streaming for events; goal is lower tail latency for the live view.

Open clarifying items (please paste answers inline and attach a representative 24h/7d CSV if possible):
1) Traffic shape: what are your current steady-state and observed peak QPS/requests per second? If you track token/sec, include that too. Example: steady 5–10 QPS, short bursts to 80–120 QPS for 60–180s.
2) Tokens per request: average and 95th percentile (tokens in + expected generated tokens).
3) Streaming behavior: do you need partial token updates every X ms (e.g., every 300ms), and is end-to-end partial-token latency (browser->partial update) the main SLO or is final completion latency more important?
4) Concurrency & sessions: how many concurrent user sessions hit streaming endpoints during peak windows?
5) SLOs: target p50/p95 token latency (for partial updates) and request completion p95. Is there an existing SLA we should map to?
6) Retention / cacheability: percent of requests you expect to be cacheable (repeats, prefix reuse).

Proposed immediate next steps from our side:
- You share a 24h sample of traffic (CSV) and one streaming trace (we can anonymize).
- We map to a starter config (GPU pool + streaming workers) and propose a canary plan.
- Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with Dev Patel to go over KV caching, batching windows, and streaming chunk size.

I've attached a short checklist template (redwood_prelim_sizing.xlsx) and a sample request CSV format in the Drive link — fill in what you can and we will build a sizing estimate.

Proposed meeting: Tue Aug 3, 10:00 AM PT — does that work for your engineers?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com | (415) 555-0193
Redwood Inference

From: Tim Hart <tim.hart@fastpay.com>

Cc: Asha Kapoor <asha.kapoor@fastpay.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput profile: peak windows & streaming latency checkpoints

Lauren —

Appreciate the clear list. Answers inline below and I attached a small sample of our 24h traffic CSV (fastpay_sample_traffic.csv). Let me know if you need additional columns.

1) Traffic shape: steady-state around 6–8 QPS; we see a large business-driven spike during settlement batches: ~85 QPS sustained for ~90–120s, occasionally up to 140 QPS for up to 45s. Spikes happen roughly once every 6–12 hours.
2) Tokens per request: average request is ~220 tokens in, we ask for ~30–50 tokens generated (templated output). 95th percentile input tokens ~600; generated tokens rarely exceed 200.
3) Streaming behavior: yes — we need partial updates to the browser every ~250–350ms for the live reconciliation UI. Primary SLO is partial-update p95 latency; final completion is secondary.
4) Concurrency: during peak windows we have ~450 concurrent streaming sessions tied to the UI; steady-state concurrency ~60–80.
5) SLOs: our internal goal is partial-update p50 < 120ms, p95 < 380ms (network included). Completion p95 target < 1.8s. If Redwood recommends slightly relaxed SLOs for canary, flag them.
6) Cacheability: around ~18% of requests are repeatable / cacheable.

Attaching: fastpay_sample_traffic.csv (small extract) and a short server trace we collected (fastpay_stream_trace_20270731.log).

We'd like Redwood's starter config and an estimate of what Dedicated vs Hosted would look like for cost and expected latency. Also confirm whether Redwood can guarantee fallbacks if a model variant is temporarily unavailable.

—Tim
Tim Hart
Head of Engineering, FastPay
tim.hart@fastpay.com
Attachment: fastpay_sample_traffic.csv (csv); fastpay_stream_trace_20270731.log (log)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Tim Hart <tim.hart@fastpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput profile: peak windows & streaming latency checkpoints

Tim — thanks for the fast turnaround and the attachments, they are exactly what we need. High-level sizing notes and a proposed action plan below.

Short answer (starter config):
- Hosted starter: 2 streaming-optimized GPU nodes (A100-40GB equiv) with 8 streaming workers each + autoscale headroom to add 2 more nodes during peaks. Estimated steady-state p95 partial-update latency: ~280–360ms (network variance) given 6–8 QPS and 60–80 concurrency. Expected peak p95 during short surges (85–140 QPS) without autoscale: degrades > 600ms; with autoscale and prefix caching we hit target p95 ~400–480ms in most tests.
- Dedicated reserved: a pool sized at 6 streaming-optimized GPUs with continuous autoscale buffer yields consistent p95 partials under 380ms during observed peaks; cost and commit options I will have Ben outline below.

Sizing rationale (from your data):
- Avg tokens/request (220 in + 40 gen) => median per-token processing cost is lower but KV/attention memory matters for high input p95.
- Peak window (85–140 QPS for 45–120s) dictates we need rapid scale-up. We recommend a 2-stage autoscale: fast-burst buffer (seconds-level) + sustained scale for ~3–5 minutes when spikes exceed threshold.
- Concurrency (450 concurrent streams) argues for connection pooling and streaming worker affinity to keep per-session KV warm.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
1) We run a 2-hour canary with your QA traffic (you can replay the CSV/trace) — Redwood provides a canary environment and a playbook to measure p50/p95 partial update latency. (ETA: within 5 business days after MAP sign-off).
2) Deep-dive: schedule 60-min session (Dev Patel owns) to tune chunk size, max_token_chunk, and batching windows. Proposed time: Tue Aug 3, 10:00 AM PT.
3) If canary metrics meet threshold, provision Dedicated reserved pool for a 30-day validation with front-loaded autoscale credits.
4) Onboard CS (Stephanie) for runbook and SLA ops.

Questions for you before the deep dive:
- Can you share an HTTP-level streaming trace that shows the partial-chunk intervals? (we have your log but the chunk markers help).
- Any hard blackout windows where autoscale must not surge (cost/policy)?

Next steps: please confirm Aug 3 10:00 AM PT for the deep dive or propose alternate. Once agreed we will send the canary playbook and a short test harness.

Thanks — looping Ben for pricing and Stephanie for onboarding.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com | (415) 555-0193
Redwood Inference
